title: The Missing Prototype
summary: Sometime between Friday evening and Saturday morning, the Argus-7 prototype vanished from a locked storage room inside Halden Dynamics. No forced entry. No witnesses. Five people had the means. One of them is lying.
briefing: Halden Dynamics is a mid-sized electronics firm on the edge of the city. Its crown jewel is the Argus-7: a solid-state memory cartridge the size of a paperback, years ahead of anything on the market.

At 07:30 on Saturday 10 March, chief engineer Dr. Maren Voss opened Storage Room B and found the Argus-7 case empty. The door showed no sign of force. The building's security systems recorded a gap in the night.
The board has asked you to work the case quietly. Review the evidence, question the five people who were in the building, rebuild the night minute by minute, and name the person responsible.
objectives: Examine the physical and documentary evidence.
Reconstruct the timeline of Friday night.
Connect clues and expose contradictions in the statements.
Form a theory and submit your conclusion.
teaser: A prototype worth a company vanishes from a locked room. No forced entry. Five people had the means.

clock.deadlineNote: The board wants a name by midnight.

file.title: Incident report
body: Halden Dynamics is a mid-sized electronics firm on the edge of the city. Its crown jewel is the Argus-7: a solid-state memory cartridge the size of a paperback, years ahead of anything on the market.

At 07:30 on Saturday 10 March, chief engineer Dr. Maren Voss opened Storage Room B and found the Argus-7 case empty. The door showed no sign of force. The building's security systems recorded a gap in the night.
The board has asked you to work the case quietly. Review the evidence, question the five people who were in the building, rebuild the night minute by minute, and name the person responsible.
Taken: the Argus-7 prototype, from its case in Storage Room B. Discovered 07:30 Saturday by Dr. Maren Voss. The door shows no sign of force.

file.title: Scene examination: Storage Room B
body: The contract locksmith examined the door at 09:05. Strike plate, deadbolt and hinges are undamaged, and the magnetic-card reader shows no tampering. Whoever opened it used a valid card.
Note for the investigating officer: the reader keeps its own log of every card used. The printouts are held by Facilities, who will release them against this report's reference, 047-2.

file.title: Persons of interest
body: Dr. Maren Voss, Chief Engineer. Designed the Argus-7; found the case empty. Usually at her bench in the Main Laboratory.
Alex Reyes, Senior Lab Technician. Calibrates the prototype; holds a card for Storage Room B. Works in the Main Laboratory.
Victor Lang, Managing Director. Master card to every door. Keeps to the Executive Office.
Nina Okafor, Night Security Officer. On the lobby desk Friday night. Can be found at the Lobby & Security Desk.
Daniel Cho, Communications Technician. Maintains the CCTV recorders and the modem bank. Works from the Communications Room.

file.title: Forensics
body: Latent prints on the Argus-7 case: several of Dr. Voss's, as expected. One clear, fresh partial on the inside latch matches Alex Reyes. It sits over a smear consistent with a glove.
His last logged handling of the case was Thursday afternoon.
